subject: Stakeholder mapping and next steps: Beta Retail procurement & security intros
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@beta-retail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder mapping and next steps: Beta Retail procurement & security intros

Jordan — great to connect earlier today. Thanks for the time and for walking through Beta Retail's use case for customer support summarization and search. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: multi-channel support summarization + semantic search for support knowledge base.
- Success criteria: 80% reduction in average handle time for support reps; latency < 300ms for 95th pct tokens in prod; predictable cost per 1M messages.
- Current blockers: procurement/PO process, security questionnaire, and decision maker alignment.

Requested next actions:
1) Stakeholder map: could you share a short org chart or list of decision makers/stakeholders (economic buyer, procurement contact, security/compliance owner, platform/infra contact)? A simple PDF or doc is perfect.
2) Intro chain: if you’re able, an intro to the procurement and security leads would speed things up — we’ll keep the outreach focused to technical/contract items only.
3) Timeline: any internal timeline for vendor selection and pilot (target month)?

Attached is our concise sales deck for context and a short checklist we use for vendor reviews. We can keep things light on the legal/security side initially and only open the questionnaire once procurement signals green.

Files attached: redwood-salesdeck.pdf (2MB, stub)

If helpful, I can propose a mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out milestones and owners. Happy to schedule a quick follow-up next week with Alex (solutions engineer) if you want a deep-dive on latency and integration.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@beta-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Li Chen <l.chen@beta-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping and next steps: Beta Retail procurement & security intros

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap.

I've attached a quick org chart with the likely stakeholders and a suggested intro chain. High level:
- Economic buyer: Maya Patel (VP, Customer Ops) — ultimate sign-off on pilot spend
- Procurement: Li Chen (Procurement Manager) — PO and contracting
- Security/Compliance: Sam Rivera (Head of Security) — will own the questionnaire and any SOC2 evidence requests
- Platform/Infra: Jordan Mills (Director, Engineering Ops) — will evaluate integration and latency requirements

Attachment: beta_retail-org-chart.pdf

Timeline: we’re aiming to select a vendor and kick off a pilot in mid-May. Procurement will want a standard SOW and PO; Li handles our vendor terms. I’ll let Li and Sam know you’ll reach out.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Director, Product Insights | Beta Retail
j.ellis@beta-retail.com | +1 212-555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping and next steps: Beta Retail procurement & security intros

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the org chart and the timeline. Appreciate the clarity on owners.

Rishi (solutions architect) and Alex (SE) are looped in to handle the technical and security questions; Neha (our enterprise AE lead) will support procurement and contracting. Quick plan from our side:
- Rishi/Alex: will prepare a 30-min technical follow-up focused on integration, expected latency, and token-cost estimates.
- Neha: will review PO/terms cadence and prepare a redline-friendly SOW template.
- I’ll draft a short MAP and send it to Maya and Li for approval — it will include milestones for Eval, Pilot, and Prod.

Jordan — when you intro Li and Sam, the key asks we’ll have up front are:
- Procurement: PO lead, standard payment/PO terms, sample vendor contract if available, billing contact
- Security: expected timeline for questionnaires, any required evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary), and whether an NDA is needed before sharing logs/sample data

Proposed next step: Jordan, can you introduce Li Chen and Sam Rivera to this thread or via a short intro email by end of day? If mid-May pilot is the target, we should lock procurement steps this month.

Thanks all —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — thanks for the org chart and timeline. Quick intro note from my side and a short checklist to make procurement and security reviews smoother: 

Hi Jordan, Sam, Li, Maya — I’m Rishi Malhotra, Solutions Architect at Redwood Inference. I’ll own the technical/security integration questions and can coordinate any narrows on latency/cost for your pilot.

To accelerate the procurement and security review, it would help to get the following items up front (we can iterate after the intro):
- Procurement: sample vendor contract or key terms, billing contact, PO process and lead time, any required insurance language or addenda.
- Security: preferred questionnaire format (SIG, proprietary), a target date to return the filled questionnaire, and any required evidence (SOC 2 Type II, pen test summary). We can provide our SOC 2 artifact and a short security whitepaper.

Attachment: security-checklist.pdf (stub)

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Jordan: intro to Li and Sam on this thread if possible.
2) Rishi/Alex: schedule a 30-min technical session next week (I’m open Tue/Wed mornings PT).
3) Neha: I’ll sync with procurement on typical SOW redlines so the SOW can be shared quickly.

Happy to keep the initial scope tight for the pilot (support summarization only) so reviews are quicker. Thanks and looking forward to the intros.

—Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
